name: Third and mixed conditionals; wish
subtitle: Use if + past perfect + would have + past participle for the past, which you cannot change: If I had known, I would have come. Use wish + past simple for a regret about now, and wish + past perfect for a regret about the past.
source: icanspeak Spanish original English text (grammar-b2 run, 2026-10-29)

concept.exampleHtml: If I had known, I would have come. — I wish I had listened.

qa.html: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle. Use it for an imaginary situation in the past. It did not happen, and now you cannot change it. If I had known about the strike, I would have taken a taxi. We would have won if we had played better. The past perfect here only shows that the situation is not real.

Mixed conditionals mix a past and a present time. Past cause, present result: if + past perfect, would + verb. If I had taken that job, I would be rich now. Present state, past result: if + past simple, would have + past participle. If Amira spoke French, she would have got the job.

wish / if only + past simple is for a regret about now. I wish I had a car. I wish I lived nearer. If only I knew the answer! wish / if only + past perfect is for a regret about the past. I wish I had listened to you. If only we had booked earlier! The tense goes one step back, like in a conditional.

wish + would shows that you are annoyed about what someone does, or that you want it to change. I wish you would knock before you come in. I wish it would stop raining. Do not use it for yourself: ✗ I wish I would be taller. → ✓ I wish I were taller.

Typical mistakes: ✗ If I would have known, I would have come. → ✓ If I had known, I would have come. (no would have in the if part) · ✗ I wish I would have more time. → ✓ I wish I had more time. · ✗ I wish I would have listened. → ✓ I wish I had listened.

concept.noteHtml: In speech, 'd can be would or had: If I'd known, I'd have come. After wish and if only, were is the careful form for I, he, she, it: I wish I were taller. Was is also common in speech. should have shows regret or criticism about the past too: You should have called me. = I wish you had called me. For the zero, first and second conditional, see Zero, first and second conditional. For could and might in the result part, see Modal verbs.

boxes.badge: No would after if or wish
items: ✗ If I would have known, … → ✓ If I had known, …
✗ I wish I would have more time. → ✓ I wish I had more time.
✗ I wish I would have gone. → ✓ I wish I had gone.
Would belongs to the result part, or to wish + someone else.
If I'd known, I'd have come. — 'd = had, then would
She wouldn't have left if he'd asked.
should have + past participle = regret about the past

listen.note: A regret about the past: wish + past perfect.

rounds.label: 1 · wish + past simple
rounds.instruction: You hear how things are. Say the wish about now: I wish + past simple.

example.answer: I wish I had a car.

items.prompt: I can't swim.
I live far from work.
items.answer: I wish I lived closer to work.

items.prompt: I don't know the answer.
items.answer: I wish I knew the answer.

items.prompt: I have to work today.
items.answer: I wish I didn't have to work today.

items.prompt: My flat doesn't have a balcony.
items.answer: I wish my flat had a balcony.

items.prompt: I don't speak Italian.

rounds.label: 2 · Third conditional
rounds.instruction: You hear what did not happen, and what happened. Say what would have been different: If + past perfect, would have.

example.prompt: I didn't leave early. I missed the train.
example.answer: If I had left early, I wouldn't have missed the train.

items.prompt: Priya didn't take a coat. She got cold.
items.answer: If Priya had taken a coat, she wouldn't have got cold.

items.prompt: We didn't book a table. We waited an hour.
items.answer: If we had booked a table, we wouldn't have waited an hour.

items.prompt: Liam lost his phone. He didn't call us.
items.answer: If Liam hadn't lost his phone, he would have called us.

items.prompt: Olga didn't check the map. She got lost.
items.answer: If Olga had checked the map, she wouldn't have got lost.

items.prompt: Diego didn't hear the alarm. He was late.
items.answer: If Diego had heard the alarm, he wouldn't have been late.

items.prompt: I didn't eat breakfast. I felt dizzy.
items.answer: If I had eaten breakfast, I wouldn't have felt dizzy.

exercises.title: Choose the right form.
exercises.hint: Past situation: if + past perfect, would have + past participle. Wish about now: past simple. Wish about the past: past perfect.
exercises.hintHtml: third conditionalif + past perfect, would have + past participle.wish, nowwish + past simple.wish, pastwish + past perfect.

items.prompt: If I ___ the news, I would have told you.
items.why: Third conditional: the if part uses the past perfect, never would have.

items.prompt: If we had left earlier, we ___ the train.
items.why: It is about a past situation, so the result part needs would have + past participle.

items.prompt: If Kwame had taken that job, he ___ in London now.
items.why: Now shows the result is in the present: mixed conditional, would + verb.

items.prompt: I'm very shy. If I ___ more confident, I would have asked for a pay rise last year.
items.why: Being shy is true now. For a present state in a mixed conditional, use the past simple: were.

items.prompt: We would have stayed longer if it ___ so cold.
items.why: Would have stayed is a third conditional, so the if part needs the past perfect.

items.prompt: I wish I ___ more time to study.
items.why: A wish about now uses the past simple: had.

items.prompt: I wish I ___ to the party last night.
items.why: Last night is the past, so a wish about it uses the past perfect.

items.prompt: It's very loud. I wish you ___ turn the music down.
items.why: You want someone else to change what they do: wish + would.

items.prompt: If only I ___ your advice last year!
items.why: Last year is the past, so a wish about it uses the past perfect.

exercises.title: Which pattern is it?
exercises.hint: Look at the verb forms. Third: past → past. Mixed: past → now or now → past. Wish: now, past or would.
